title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The ambient group is G+ = SL(2,Z)^, the profinite completion of SL(2,Z). Its generators are rho (order 6) and sigma (order 4), with rho^3 = sigma^2 = -1. The centre is mu = {1, rho^3} = {1, sigma^2}.

On the previous pages Grothendieck defines a group Z_{rho,sigma}. Its elements are quadruples (u, chi, eps2, eps3) in which u is an automorphism of G+ subject to conditions a)-d) relative to a normal subgroup G^q of G+:
- u(rho) is conjugate to rho^{eps3};
- u(sigma) is conjugate to sigma^{eps2};
- the conjugating elements are compatible modulo G^q (conditions a), b));
- condition d) concerns the action on G+/G^q.

This is a 'modular' (genus-1, M_{1,1}) avatar of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller-type groups. M(0), M[0], M^![0] are his GT-like groups. L_0 is the procyclic subgroup generated by a parabolic element eps_0; it acts by inner automorphisms.

He computes Z for several choices of G^q:
- (a) G^q = G+ gives Z = M[0].
- (b) G^q = Pi = Pi_0 x mu, the completed principal congruence subgroup Gamma(2)^, gives Z = M^![0]. Here Pi_0 is free profinite of rank 2, i.e. pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, and G+/Pi maps to S_3.

This page treats case (c), G^q = Pi_0:
- Conditions a), b) are unchanged, since mu is central, but d) becomes stricter.
- One finds Z ∩ G+ = L_0^{Pi_0}, of index 2 in L_0^{Pi} from case (b).
- M(0) (or M^!) acts on G+/Pi_0 through the character eps2^*.
- Hence Z = M''(0).L_0^{Pi_0} = M''[0]_0, where M'' denotes the kernel of eps2 : M -> mu (formula 15).

Marginal notes discuss this. With a modification of condition d) (the marginal condition attached to (14)), one recovers Z = M^![0] as in case (b). So the result is 'not too small', whereas the naive definition gives the index-2 subgroup.

General lesson (16)-(17): whenever G^q splits as G^q_0 x mu, with G^q_0 independent of the choices, one should define Z in terms of G^q_0. One should also pick the conjugating elements alpha, beta of definition (14) in G^q_{0,tau} := mu_tau . G^q_0.

Final remark: the simpler definition of p. 578 (G^q ⊂ Pi, trivial action on G+/Pi) forces, as the next page explains, eps3 = 1. The reason is that rho^{-1} ≠ rho, and u(rho) is conjugate to rho^{eps3} in G+ but not in general by elements of Pi.

Purpose: to find the right definition of a Teichmüller-type group Z_{rho,sigma}, and of its quotient Gamma_{rho,sigma} = Z/L_0^G (defined on the next page), that is stable under change of the congruence level G^q. This is bookkeeping of index-2 phenomena coming from the centre mu and from the signs eps2, eps3.
errors: No clear mathematical error. The computation that the strict version of condition d) cuts Z down to the kernel of eps2 is consistent with M acting on G+/Pi_0 (a group of order 12) through eps2.
The page is a working draft: the marginal notes revise the definition rather than correct a computation. The final status of condition d) is left to later pages.
The transcription's 'Z_{ς,σ}' and 'G^ς' are misreadings of Z_{rho,sigma} and G^q.

ideas.what: Z_{rho,sigma}: automorphisms of SL(2,Z)^ preserving the conjugacy classes of rho and sigma up to signs eps3 and eps2, compatibly modulo a normal subgroup G^q; computed for G^q = G+, Pi = Gamma(2)^, and Pi_0
ideas.modern_name: Genus-1 / SL2(Z)^ (M_{1,1}) version of the Grothendieck-Teichmüller group; variants of GT-hat
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (GT, 1990); Ihara; Lochak-Schneps and Nakamura for genus-1 and SL2(Z)-type actions; Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps
ideas.where_published: Spirit sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, M_{1,1}, SL2(Z)^); details only in these unpublished notes

ideas.what: Index-2 subgroups M''(0) = Ker(eps2) and M''[0]_0 arising when the congruence level passes from Pi = Pi_0 x mu to Pi_0
ideas.modern_name: Index-2 subgroups of GT-type groups cut out by sign characters

ideas.what: Principle: if G^q = G^q_0 x mu with G^q_0 canonical, define the group via G^q_0 and take the conjugating elements in mu_tau.G^q_0
ideas.modern_name: Splitting off the centre ±1 (passing from SL2 to PSL2-level data)

deep.surprise_reason: This is technical bookkeeping on the definition of a genus-1 GT-type group (index-2 issues caused by the centre ±1 and the signs eps2, eps3). The broader program (GT acting on SL2(Z)^ via rho and sigma) is unpublished in this detail, but its essence is known from Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura and others. The page contains no standalone new result.
transcription_corrections: '𝔊^ς' should read 𝔊^q, the congruence-level subgroup (the same symbol as on the previous page).
'π_0' and 'π' should read Π_0 and Π (as on the previous page).
'631' at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination; the archive page is 656.
The interlinear 'M^!' above 'M(0)' is an alternative ('M(0) [ou M^!] sur 𝔊^+/Π_0').
(16) the parenthetical reads roughly '(ici pour les sous-groupes contenant μ = {1,ρ^3} = {1,σ^2})'.
The left oblique margin speaks of M^{Π_0}[0] = M[0]_0 = M(0).L_0^{Π_0}; the 'M(0).π_0' in the transcription is likely M(0).L_0^{Π_0}.
